building.name: Coffee Shop (Hawthorne Grill / Spires-type Diner)
building.note: A normal Denny's, Spires-like coffee shop in Los Angeles. Modeled after the type of diner common in 1990s Southern California — rectangular, single-story, flat roof, large windows, booths along the perimeter, counter seating, visible kitchen.

floors.name: Ground Floor
floors.note: Single-story diner. Floor-to-floor height of 3.6m accommodates the dropped ceiling at ~2.7m with MEP plenum above.

openings.note: Large plate glass window — south facade, booth seating side. Morning sun streams in.
Second south window — Pumpkin and Honey Bunny's booth is near here.
Main entrance — glass double doors, south facade.
South window — dining area east end.

walls.note: South exterior wall — main facade with large diner windows and entrance.

openings.note: Service pass-through from dining to kitchen corridor.
Wide service opening — order window / food pass.

walls.note: Main partition wall separating dining area (south) from kitchen/back-of-house (north). The counter runs along the dining side of this wall.
Partition between men's and women's restrooms.

spaces.name: Main Dining Area
spaces.note: The main dining room. About 9:00 in the morning. While the place isn't jammed, there's a healthy number of people drinking coffee, munching on bacon and eating eggs. Booths line the south and east window walls. Freestanding tables and chairs fill the center. The counter with swivel stools runs along the north partition wall. Pumpkin and Honey Bunny sit in a booth along the south windows.

spaces.name: Kitchen
spaces.note: Commercial kitchen — grill line, prep area, dish pit. The Cook works the flat-top grill. Visible through the food pass window from the dining area. Stainless steel surfaces, exhaust hood over the grill line.

spaces.name: Waitress Station / Service Corridor
spaces.note: Service station — coffee maker, soda fountain, order tickets. The Waitress comes by with a pot of coffee from here. Coffee pots on warmers, stacks of mugs.

spaces.name: Storage / Dry Goods
spaces.note: Back-of-house dry storage. Shelving with canned goods, coffee supplies, napkins, etc.

slabs.note: Ground floor slab on grade — 150mm reinforced concrete.
Roof deck — steel deck with concrete topping. Dropped ceiling below at 2.7m.

structuralElements.note: Interior column — steel W-shape, supporting roof structure.

fixtures.note: Long Formica counter with chrome-and-vinyl swivel stools. Runs along the kitchen partition wall. The Waitress pours coffee here. Classic diner counter — napkin dispensers, sugar caddies, ketchup bottles.

fixtures.label: Freestanding Table 1

fixtures.label: Cash Register / Hostess Station

metadata.note: 3D building model of the coffee shop from the opening scene of Pulp Fiction (1994), written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. Modeled as a Denny's/Spires-type diner in Los Angeles, circa 1994. The scene features Pumpkin (Tim Roth) and Honey Bunny (Amanda Plummer) in a booth, planning and then executing a robbery. The Waitress serves coffee. Patrons eat Denver omelets. 'Everybody be cool this is a robbery!' The building is a single-story, flat-roof commercial restaurant — 24m × 14m — with booths along the window walls, a long counter with swivel stools, a visible kitchen, and restrooms in the back corner.

closing_lines.honey_bunny: Any of you fuckin' pricks move and I'll execute every one of you motherfuckers! Got that?
